P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Not established from a captured source. The Law on Currency Settlements governs FX; domestic pricing and settlement must generally be in tugrik, with cross-border transactions reportedly excepted. No surrender requirement for individuals' foreign receipts was found.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Mongolbank's translation of the Law on Currency Settlements was captured without the tugrik-settlement/exception text on 2026-10-22.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Mongolian banks hold USD for individuals; for example, Golomt Bank's salary current account is offered in MNT or USD (no interest, free to open). The Law on Currency Settlements governs banks' handling of customers' foreign-currency accounts (see P1).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents pay a flat 20% on Mongolian-source income. Residence applies to anyone present 183 days or more in 12 consecutive months, or with 50% or more of taxable income from Mongolian sources. Employment and similar income is taxed at 10% up to MNT 120m, 15% from MNT 120–180m and 20% above (PwC). Per TaxAtlas, business income is also subject to the progressive rates, and its top rate (25%) conflicts with PwC.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 10%. Taxpayers, including individuals, whose sales reach MNT 50 million or more within 12 consecutive months must register as VAT withholders; voluntary registration is possible from MNT 10 million. Services received from non-residents are subject to reverse-charge VAT. PwC's wording lists exported supplies under the 10% rate, and zero-rating of exported services was not confirmed.
L4_vat_gst.note: Single secondary domain (PwC) captured on 2026-10-22; a 2025 PwC alert on draft laws (MNT 400m threshold) returned 403.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Law on Personal Data Protection (passed 17 December 2021, reportedly in force 1 May 2022) regulates the collection, processing, use and security of personal data by persons, legal entities and non-legal entities. It replaced the 1995 Law on Personal Secrecy. Consent, data-subject rights and breach notification are reported features.
L5_data_protection.note: Official translation captured (scope only); dates from search summaries (PwC alert 403, IAPP page without body) on 2026-10-22.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
